﴿So leave them﴾ and let them be, paying them no mind. This is a command to disengage from them, and it is abrogated (منسوخ, *mansukh*, meaning superseded by a later ruling, *naskh*) by the verse of the sword. ﴿Until they meet﴾: Abu Haywa read it as يُلْقُوا (*yulqū*), the imperfect of لَقِيَ (*laqiya*, "to meet"). ﴿their day in which they will be struck senseless﴾ is read in the passive, يُصْعَقُونَ (*yuṣ'aqūn*), by ʿAsim, Ibn ʿAmir, Zayd ibn ʿAli, and the people of Mecca according to Shibl ibn ʿIbad, who said: "مَن صَعَقَتْهُ الصّاعِقَةُ" (*man ṣaʿaqathu al-ṣāʿiqah*, "whom the thunderbolt has struck senseless") or "مَن أصْعَقَتْهُ" (*man aṣ'aqathu*, "whom [someone] has struck senseless"). The majority, and the people of Mecca according to Isma'il, read it as يَصْعَقُونَ (*yaṣ'aqūn*) with a fatḥa on the yā' and ʿayn, while al-Sulami read it with a ḍammah on the yā' and a kasrah on the ʿayn, from أصْعَقَ (*aṣ'aqa*), the causative form with four root letters.

The intended day is the day of Badr. It has also been said that it is the time of the First Blast, since on it everyone in the heavens and everyone on the earth will be struck senseless. This has been objected to: only those who are alive at that time are struck senseless, and these people are not such, and that

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 52, verse 46:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day when their plotting will avail them nothing﴾, i.e., nothing of availing, is a substitute (badal) for "their day." It is not hidden that the explicit statement of the uselessness of their plotting calls for their employing it, hoping to benefit from it. And this is nothing other than the scheme they devised concerning the matter of the Prophet, may Allah exalt him and grant him peace, among which was their opposition on the Day of Badr. As for the first blast (al-nafkhah al-ula), it is not among the things that are used to repel plotting and stratagems. It has been answered regarding the first point: by denying that the swoon (al-sa'q) is restricted to the living, for the dead also swoon, and they are included in the generality of "man" (man), even though their swooning is not like the swooning of the living in every respect; and this is contrary to the apparent meaning, so it requires a sound transmission. As for the second point, the speech is in the manner of his saying, "ʿAlā lā ḥubba lā yuhtadā bi-manārihi" (Upon one who has no love, whose beacon is not followed), so the meaning is: the Day when there will be for them neither plotting nor availing. This is frequent in the Qur'an and is one of the gates of eloquence and excellence. It has been said that it is the Day of Resurrection, and this is the view of the majority, though there is a discussion concerning it. It has also been said that it is the Day of their death, but this was objected to, on the grounds that there is what there is in it, along with the fact that the idafah (genitive construction), which indicates its being specific to them, repels it; so do not overlook this. ﴿Nor will they be helped﴾: from the side of another, in repelling the punishment from them.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 52, verse 47:

﴿And indeed, for those who have done wrong﴾ — that is, for them. The relative pronoun (al-mawsul) has been placed in the position of the pronoun because of what was mentioned before it. It is also permitted that the meaning is general, with them included in it in a primary way. ﴿a punishment﴾ — another one — ﴿short of that﴾ — short of what they encountered of killing; that is, before it. And it is, as Mujahid said, the drought that afflicted them for seven years.

And from Ibn Abbas: it is what was upon them on the day of Badr and the conquest (of Mecca). "Short of that" has also been explained as "before the Day of Resurrection," on the basis that their day in which they will swoon is that day. And this is also from him. And from al-Bara' ibn Azib: that it is the punishment of the grave. This is built upon a similar interpretation to that one, and some scholars held it on the basis that "short of that" means "beyond that," as in the verse of the poet:

"It shows you the mote from beyond them, while it is beneath them."

If the day is explained as the Day of Resurrection or similar, and "short of that" as "before it," and the relative pronoun is taken in its general sense, then this punishment is the punishment of the grave, or the worldly calamities. In the codex of Abdullah, the reading is "short of that" in an approximate sense. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ — that the matter is as mentioned. In this is an indication that among them are those who know it, but they persist in disbelief out of obstinacy, or that they do not act upon anything.

**Ruh al-Ma'ani (al-Alusi), on Surah 52, verse 48:**

﴿And be patient for the judgment of your Lord﴾: by His giving them respite until their promised day, and by your remaining among them while enduring sorrows and bearing anxieties. ﴿Indeed, you are under Our eyes﴾: that is, under Our protection and safeguarding. Here "eye" is a metaphor (majaz) for protection, and it is also used figuratively for the one who protects, which is a well-known metaphor. In al-Kashshaf, it is said that the phrase means "such that We see you and keep you safe." The word "eyes" is in the plural here because it is attached to a plural pronoun, whereas in Surah Ta-Ha it is in the singular because it is attached to a singular pronoun. Al-Zamakhshari, in Surah al-Mu'minun, hinted that the purpose of the plural is to indicate intensity in protection, as if with Him, exalted is He, there were guardians who keep watch with their eyes. Al-Allama al-Tayyibi said: "He used the singular there to match the singular verb, which is the guarding (kila'ah) of Musa, peace be upon him. Here, since it is for consoling the Beloved (ﷺ) regarding the plots and the hardships of the duties and acts of obedience, the plural is suitable, because these are many actions, each of which requires guarding from Him, glorified and exalted is He." End of quotation. Whoever looks with the eye of insight will recognise from the two verses the difference between the Beloved (ﷺ) and the interlocutor (Musa), upon both of them be the best of blessings and the fullest of peace.

Discussion of similar expressions according to the method of the salaf (the early generations) is well known. Abu al-Sammal read "bi-a'yunna" with a doubled nun.

﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise﴾: that is, say "Glory be to Allah" while combining it with praise of Him for His blessings, which cannot be counted. The meaning is: glorify Him, exalted is He, and praise Him. ﴿When you arise﴾: from every gathering. This is the view of Ata', Mujahid and Ibn Jubayr. It is authentically reported in the narrations of Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and others, from Abu Barzah al-Aslami, that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say, when he wished to rise from a gathering:

"Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You. I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance."

He was asked about this, and he said: "It is an expiation for what occurs in the gathering." There are many reports on this.

It has also been said: "When you arise" means when you arise for prayer. Abu Ubayd and Ibn al-Mundhir reported from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: "It is a duty upon every Muslim, when he arises for prayer, to say: 'Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him,' because Allah, exalted is He, says to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise when you arise.﴾" Sa'id ibn Mansur and others reported from al-Dahhak that he said about the verse:

"When you arise for prayer, say these words: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.'" This is related in al-Bahr from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Mardawayh reported from him that he said: "Glorify your Lord with His praise when you rise from your bed until you enter into the prayer." Something similar is narrated from Ibn al-Sa'ib. Zayd ibn Aslam said: "When you rise from the midday rest (qa'ilah), and the glorification at that time is the Dhuhr prayer."

**Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 52, verse 49 (part 1 of 2):**

God's words: ﴿And during part of the night, glorify Him﴾ single out a portion of the night for glorification, because worship at that time is harder on the soul and further from showing off (riya'), as is hinted at by placing it before the verb. ﴿And at the retreat of the stars﴾ means at the time of their retreat at the end of the night, that is, their disappearance with the light of dawn. It is also said that "glorifying during the night" means the Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers, and ﴿the retreat of the stars﴾ means the two rak'ahs of Fajr. It is reported from 'Umar (may God be pleased with him), 'Ali (may God ennoble his face), Abu Hurayrah and al-Hasan (may God be pleased with them both) that "glorifying during the night" refers to the voluntary prayers, and ﴿the retreat of the stars﴾ to the two rak'ahs of Fajr.

[p. 41]

Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, al-Minhal ibn 'Amr and Ya'qub read *adbar* (أدبار) with a fatha on the hamza. It is the plural of *dubur* (دبر), meaning "behind/aftermath," so the sense is "in the aftermath of them," i.e., when they set, or when they are hidden by the rays of the sun.

Now, the arrangement of the verses from God's words ﴿Or do they say, "He is a poet"?﴾ [al-Tur: 30] to His words, glorified is He: ﴿Or do they have a god other than God?﴾ and so on, contains something strange. I have not seen anyone uncover its veil as the author of al-Kashshaf did, may God reward him well. Because of its excellence, and because nothing can be added to it, I wished to quote it in full, though with some abridgment. I say, then:

He (al-Zamakhshari) said: Al-Zamakhshari alluded to two aspects in God's words: ﴿Nay, they say, "Confused dreams!" Nay, he has invented it! Nay, he is a poet﴾ [al-Anbiya': 5]. One is that it is a report of their confused statement as it stands, and the second is that it is a gradual progression by God, glorified is He, in relating what they said of the denial toward what they are immersed in. The first is weak in our context, because what the speech is directed at is not the confusion of their statements, so that it would be reported as it is. Rather it is consolation for him (ﷺ), and that God will certainly avenge him on them, and that the punishment they denied is coming upon them as recompense for their denial of the one who announces, the announcement, and what is announced. So the second is the definite reading. Its basis, and God knows best, is that His words ﴿So remind﴾ mean: since it has been established that the punishment is coming, and that the two groups, the believers and the deniers, will be repaid for their deeds, and that you are upon the manifest truth, whoever denies it deserves humiliation, and whoever affirms it deserves approval, then persist in reminding, and do not care about what is plotted against you, for you are the one who prevails by proof and by sword in this abode, and by station and elevation in the abode of permanence. And from God's words ﴿So you are not﴾ to His words, glorified is He: ﴿they are the ones who plot﴾ comes the detailed explanation of this summary, together with an allusion to the corruption of their foolish sayings, and that they are in plain view of God and within His hearing, so He will certainly avenge His Prophet (ﷺ) upon them. In this there is also that the Prophet (ﷺ) has a rank with God that cannot be measured, so it strengthens the arm of consolation. And God's words, glorified is He: ﴿So you are not, by the grace of your Lord﴾ [al-Tur: 29], etc., contain that one upon whom prophethood has been bestowed cannot be either of these two. He began with their contradictory saying in order first to alert to the corruption of their opinions, and to make it a rule for their turning away from the truth and preferring to follow their desires. How far is the condition of one who was the most sound in judgment, the most balanced in intellect, and the clearest in signs, from the time he grew up until he reached maturity, from madness and soothsaying! Moreover, the two are contradictory, since soothsayers were among their most accomplished people and their word was an authoritative guide among them. So where is soothsaying from madness? Then he rose to the point of their saying, that he is a poet, and God forbid that he (ﷺ) be a poet, because that is more akin to falsehood than the soothsayer or the madman. Of old it was said: the best poetry is the most false. This illustrates their stammering and confusion. God's words ﴿Say, "Wait"﴾ [al-Tur: 31] are in the manner of repaying them in kind, and in them is a completion of the threat. This is one aspect of their denial, which God first demolished by His words ﴿by the grace of your Lord﴾, and secondly explicitly by His words, may His majesty be exalted.

﴿Or do their minds command them to this?﴾ [al-Tur: 32]. It is as if it were said: leave them and that statement and its confusion, for in it there is a lesson. Then it is said: No, rather that is from their transgression, because it is more damning than a deficiency of reason, and more effective as consolation, since whoever transgresses against God, the Mighty and Majestic, has drawn His anger. Then he proceeded to a matter that goes further in denial, namely the attribution of fabrication to him (ﷺ). That is because fabrication is the furthest thing from his condition, given his renown for truthfulness. Moreover, that it is a fabrication and their inability to produce even the shortest surah like it from this "fabricator" are mutually contradictory, since that inability indicates the truth, as has passed in al-Ahqaf. Also, a poet does not deliberately lie for its own sake, and his poetry may contain wisdom and admonitions, which bring no shame. The gradation away from poetry here is the reverse of the gradation toward it in al-Anbiya', because the construction of the speech here is based on a gradation in contradiction and deepening in disparagement of him (ﷺ) and in denying his messengership. There, it was a disparagement of part of the Remembrance that is continually being revealed. So it is said: his fabrication is not far-fetched for one who is a poet with many fabrications. But where is this from that?

[p. 42]

In order to alert to the deepening, the explicit particle of retraction is used in the reply: ﴿Nay, they do not believe﴾ [al-Tur: 33], and it is followed by His words: ﴿Then let them bring﴾ [al-Tur: 34]. Then whoever does not believe denies it more strongly than the transgressor, just as the fabricator is more akin to falsehood than the poet. Then he proceeded in a more eloquent manner in replying to their claims of madness, soothsaying, which are close to each other, then poetry, then fabrication, where he treated the speakers as if they claimed that they were created from nothing, that is, without any determiner and creator. Otherwise they would have been concerned to investigate His attributes and actions, and would not have denied from you what they denied. And since they assume He is independent of any originator, they attribute His messenger to madness and soothsaying. No, rather they are like one who claims that he created himself, so there is no creator for him whose attributes he would investigate. So he attributes it to poetry, since He would not send anyone to him at all, and poetry is more akin to falsehood. No, rather they are like one who claims that he created the heavens and the earth and what is between them, so he attributes it to fabrication, since He did not send him. Then he explicitly retracted from that by His words: ﴿Nay, they are not certain﴾ [al-Tur: 36]. One who has no certainty about such an obvious matter is not far from slandering you with whatever slander. So it is as if it were said: their statement leads to this, not that they actually held these views, in order to show their persistence in obstinacy. Then it was exaggerated, and there came what indicates that the Messenger must be a fabricator, unfit for prophethood in their assumption. The first, since it did not prevent the multiplicity of gods, only indicates his fabrication in that one of two creators would not call the other to worship him. The second prevents it entirely, because if all the treasuries of his Lord were with them and they had not sent him, it would necessarily follow that he is definitely a fabricator. He also included in it their denial of the return, and their attribution of fabrication to him (ﷺ) in that matter as well, specifically. Taking it as the treasuries of power is more apparent, because ﴿Or do they have the unseen?﴾ [al-Tur: 41] refers to the treasuries of knowledge. And since the intended matter there is the issue of resurrection, as will be verified, God willing, this statement is also acceptable there. The progression in His words ﴿Or do they have control?﴾ [al-Tur: 37] is not hidden.

Then, when he finished with that and clarified (the) corruption of what they based the matter of denial upon by rational proof, it was said: nothing remains but direct observation and hearing from Him, may He be exalted, and this is more evident in its impossibility. So He mocked them. It was also said: ﴿Or do they have a ladder by which they listen?﴾ [al-Tur: 38], and it was appended with His words: ﴿Or does He have daughters?﴾ [al-Tur: 39], indicating that whoever makes his Creator inferior to himself would not find it strange that he utters such foolish statements. It is as if he (ﷺ) were being consoled. It was also said: it is enough to note the equality of the two accusations in falsehood and what they incur of evil consequences from both. Then it was said: ﴿Or do you ask them for a reward?﴾ [al-Tur: 40], meaning: these people are men of intellect, and they are not at all of those attributes. Rather, what has made them averse to you is that you ask them for a reward, whether wealth, rank, or fame. In this there is mockery of them and blame for them for envy and baseness, and that, together with their limited outlook regarding the matter of the promised day, they do not base the matter on what is customary and familiar. For no one among the people of this world and the men of great stakes would be averse to a sincere adviser who is free of the stain of greed, with such statements. Moreover, it is envy that has no effect upon those who possess it. So they are not in a position to attain the blessing of prophethood, nor is he one who covets their blessings in any of the three ways. Then it was said: ﴿Or do they have the unseen?﴾, in the sense of: rather, is the Preserved Tablet with them, so that they know everything that exists and write those known things in it? They know that what you claim about the return is not among what exists and is written. The purpose of this is to negate what is announced, namely the resurrection, in a manner that also implicitly negates prophethood, as a reverse of the first. For this reason he placed it after ﴿Or do they have a ladder?﴾, since it has been established that the target of the purpose is the discourse of the announcement, the announcer, and what is announced. So he concluded the first two with the allusion to the third, and then began with it, along with the allusion to the first two, in fulfilment of the right of inimitability. In "the unseen" there is an allusion to the unseen, namely the Hour, the first of all things. In it there is also a progression in refutation from one aspect too, because knowledge has a wider scope than power. And because the first was a denial in that they had not sent him, while this is from that aspect, and from the aspect that they did not know of the sending of anyone else to him either, despite the completeness of their knowledge. But this is not intended as the primary purpose. Then the speech ended with a turn away from denial to a report about their condition: that they intend a plot against you, so they set snares for you in word and deed.

[p. 43]

They do not stop at this statement alone, while they are themselves the ones plotted against, not you, in word and deed, in proof and sword. He fulfilled the threat contained in it with His words: ﴿Or do they have a god other than God?﴾, so that He would save them from His plot and punishment. No, by God, glory be to God above having any god other than Him. From this it appears that taking ﴿those who disbelieve﴾ to mean "those who intend a plot against him" is more apparent in this context. Concluded. What follows seems to be an emphasis on the matter of their transgression, an increase in the verification of the threat, and an exaggeration in consolation. It will be known from what he mentioned (may God's mercy continue upon him) that the particle ("or," أم) in all of this is disjunctive (munqati'ah), and it is taken as implying "rather" (bal) in its retractive sense. The retraction here occurs by way of progression, and with the hamza, which is for denial. This is what Abu al-Baqa' and many commentators chose. Al-Tha'labi related from al-Khalil that it is connective (muttasilah), and that what is meant by it is interrogation. Adhere to what the words of that great scholar have conveyed, and God knows best.

Among the allusive (ishara, esoteric indication) interpretations that they have mentioned for some verses: ﴿By the Mount﴾ is an allusion to the human frame (qalib); ﴿and a Book inscribed﴾ is an allusion to his secret (sirr); ﴿in parchment unrolled﴾ is an allusion to his heart; ﴿and the frequented House﴾ is an allusion to his spirit; ﴿and the raised canopy﴾ is an allusion to his attribute; ﴿and the sea set ablaze﴾ is an allusion to his own soul, set ablaze with the fires of desire, anger and pride. It has also been said: "al-Tur" is an allusion to the spirits that flew up from the world of holiness and the malakut (the realm of the unseen dominion), until they fell into the nets of the world of the King. "The Book inscribed in unrolled parchment" is an allusion to the divine engravings, perceived by the sight of holy insight, written upon the pages of the horizons. ﴿The frequented House﴾ is an allusion to the heart of the believer, frequented with knowledge and sincerity. ﴿The raised canopy﴾ is an allusion to the exalted world, raised above the earth of nature. ﴿The sea set ablaze﴾ is an allusion to the sea of power, filled with kinds of things decreed that have no end. It has also been said that it is an allusion to the expanse in which are the bewildered angels, and its description as "set ablaze" is either because it is filled with them, or because it has been kindled with the fires of ecstatic love (al-huyam), and for this reason none of them knows anything other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It has also been said other things.

﴿So woe on that day to those who deny﴾
﴿who are playing in vain discourse﴾: that is, they plunge into the depths of the deep worldly sea and play in it with its worthless foam and its meagre goods, and they deny those who have been purified of turbidities and adorned with lights, when they warned them that the God-fearing are the opposites of those [deniers].

﴿Enjoying what their Lord has given them﴾: of what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no thought has occurred to a human heart.
﴿And their Lord has protected them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾: and this is the punishment of veiling (hijab).

﴿Eat﴾ of the fruits of knowledge specific to the self's subtle faculty (al-latifa al-nafsiyya).
﴿And drink﴾ from the waters of the springs specific to the heart's subtle faculty (al-latifa al-qalbiyya).

﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise when you arise﴾: that is, at the station of servanthood.
﴿And glorify Him in the night﴾: that is, at the descent of tranquillity (sakina) upon you.
﴿And at the retreat of the stars﴾: that is, at the appearance of the light of the sun of the countenance. His glorification, glory be to Him, at that time consists in guarding against affirming any existence other than His existence, exalted is the Real, for affirming such [a separate existence] is absolute polytheism (shirk) in that station. May Allah, exalted is He, protect us and you from polytheism, by the sanctity of the Beloved, upon him be peace and blessings.
